newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PowerGen unit in Indonesia deal.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen unit in Indonesia deal.

text.p: A unit of PowerGen Plc, PT Power Jawa Barat, signed an agreement on Tuesday to sell power to Indonesian state electricity firm PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN) for 30 years.
"PLN will buy electricity at 6.04 U.S cents per kilowatt hour for 30 years," PLN said in a statement.
James Carmichael, PowerGen general manager for the Asia-Pacific, told Reuters the power would come from a 450 megawatt coal-fire plant in in Serang, West Java.
Construction of the plant is expected to begin in early 1998, he said.
"It's a very good price, we believe, for PLN," Carmichael said, referring to the contract. "We believe PLN has secured a fair price and we believe we've secured a fair price."
